design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (pap_therapy_rentals). Step 0 draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,4,4]; the purchase root takes 5, the two usage-summary problems take 4 each.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: pap_ext_return_labor, pap_ext_return_parts, pap_ext_used_accessories, pap_ext_self_pay_refund and the tools record_return_inspection_bc7317cd / return_device_for_refund_b6f98fe9 (pap_repair inspection + pap_purchase_refund). Claimed by task 1: pap_ext_usage_nights, pap_ext_usage_hours, pap_ext_home_unit_purchase with record_usage_download_48c54aed (agent, pap_compliance_download) and purchase_home_device_8c1f8216 (user, pap_purchase_sale) - disjoint events, tools and quantities; nothing remains unclaimed. Blueprint constraint record as in task 0: rental paid lines, pap_return and pap_claim_reversal are not written (cross-category triggers).
WHY A GOOD TEST. A Medicare patient whose coverage trial failed asks only to buy outright the Auto-Adjusting CPAP standing in his home. The purchase rule states two prerequisite sentences (state form): the price is fixed only after the device record carries a usage summary crediting the qualifying nights, and no wear is taken until a usage summary states the average daily use. The record holds three scored 30-night windows (all not_met), an in-home malfunction swap, a supplier repair and an approved pressure change, but no summary, so the agent must find the summary write, compute qualifying nights and average daily use from two separate four-factor policies (window scope by serial, swap, acclimation and pressure credits), file them in one download, and then price the unit with a five-factor rule reading the coverage status, the new summary, the trial clock, the repair history and the supply enrollment.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD. root pap_ext_home_unit_purchase (target purchase_home_device_8c1f8216, owner user). Edge 1 -> pap_ext_usage_nights, value_input, gate failed_pct, form state, sentence "The price of a unit bought where it already stands in the patient's home is fixed only after the device record carries a usage summary crediting the qualifying nights." (affirmative). Edge 2 -> pap_ext_usage_hours, value_input, gate worn_price, form state, sentence "No wear is taken off the in-home unit's price until a usage summary on the device record states the average daily use." (negated). Both resolve by record_usage_download_48c54aed (agent), the only write of this difficulty that puts a pap_compliance_download with compliance_result none on a device record. Four-point test: ordering connective only after / not ... until; record-visible state (a usage summary on the record); no tool, id or code token; hard wait scoped to the one device record. Opening evidence the state is false: the only pap_compliance_download rows (df0f671d, 8113281e, 9845aa74) carry compliance_result not_met. Order: download call (step 8, both prerequisites, no edge between them) then purchase (step 10). Deletion sensitivity: skipping step 8 makes the purchase 791.50 instead of 710.52 (no wear on the 750.00 list price, no trial discount, 5 percent repair discount, humidifier 79.00).
FACTOR CARD. NIGHTS 47 (baseline 51): serial_window_scope (method) swap D2 on record -> only scored windows from serial 23250973314 (W2 18 + W3 19 = 37) [baseline all scored windows -> 61]; swap_night_credit swap by in-home visit -> 2 [-> 45]; acclimation_night_credit first unit 23194410582 window W1 14/30 = 46.7 percent -> 5 [-> 42]; pressure_night_credit approved request f15297f9 -> 3 [-> 44]. HOURS 4.8 (baseline 4.0): serial_hours_scope (method) (4.1 + 4.3)/2 = 4.2 [all scored windows 4.0 -> 4.6]; swap_time_addback 0.2 [-> 4.6]; pressure_time_addback 0.3 [-> 4.5]; first_unit_time_addback first unit average 3.6 -> 0.1 [-> 4.7]. PURCHASE 710.52 (baseline 899.00): list_price_basis (cross-difficulty coverage) the Original Medicare Part B record the unit is rented under is active -> the class's charge for a rented device not returned, 750.00 [retail 899.00 -> 835.98]; hours_wear_basis (method) summary average 4.8 h (>= 4.5) -> 4.8 h x 134 days (2026-06-08 -> 2026-10-20) = 643.2 h over 20000 -> 725.88 [no wear -> 731.50]; failed_trial_discount (multi-source) trial period passed (134 > 90 days) and 47 credited nights (40 to 49) -> 8 percent [-> 768.59]; repair_history_discount one repair job 3aac8717 on the device record (done on the swapped-out unit, counted by the rule) -> 5 percent [-> 746.81]; humidifier_bundle_value (cross-difficulty resupply) humidifier furnished and enrollment e6456ba4 shows it in use -> 79.00 [-> 631.52]. Price = RND(725.88 x (1 - 13/100)) + 79.00 = 631.52 + 79.00 = 710.52. Near misses: the old-serial window W1 is excluded from the scope but drives the acclimation credit; a reader who stops at the not_met stamps knows the trial failed but not which of 15, 8 or 4 percent applies - only the credited count decides (47 -> 8; the uncredited current-serial sum 37 -> 15; the uncredited all-window sum 51 or all windows with credits 61 -> 4); likewise the raw window averages (4.2 current serial, 4.0 all) sit below 4.5 hours, so only the computed summary average 4.8 selects therapy-hours wear.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. pap_compliance_download and pap_purchase_sale carry no subject-scoped eligibility gate in base (pap_trial_compliance's gate applies to conversion, pap_self_pay's gates to refunds), so both writes rest on policy scope. Overwrites declared: pap_trial_compliance "A compliance download scores one window ..." superseded for the usage summary (no met/not-met result); pap_self_pay retail-plus-delivery-fee clause superseded for an in-home unit (no delivery fee). The trial status: setup 2026-06-08, trial 90 days ended 2026-09-05, no met window and no re-evaluation, so the record stays trial_active and Medicare months from 4 are not billable; the purchase is the patient's alternative to returning the unit.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: coverage-billed device record 785ef62b (serial 23250973314 now in the home), its coverage db870b3a and supply enrollment e6456ba4. Windows W1 (old serial) vs W2/W3 (new serial) are told apart by serial_number; the repair job 3aac8717 is the supplier swap behind D2.
PERSONA. Gruff retired tool-and-die maker; volunteers only the wish to buy and own the machine at home; phone to locate, DOB and ZIP on request; machine history only when asked; refuses a return if offered; runs the purchase with the price and device code given; no other ask, no prerequisite named.
STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read device, service history, requests, coverage, supply enrollment; compute nights 47 and hours 4.8 on the opening world; file the summary covering 2026-06-08 to 2026-09-19 (setup date to last night of the latest scored window) with serial 23250973314; compute the price 710.52 on the world carrying the summary; hand over the purchase with hcpcs_code E0601.
VERIFICATION (round 2, /tmp/pap_therapy_rentals_0057/verify.py): NIGHTS 47 (61, 45, 42, 44; all-baseline 51); HOURS 4.8 (4.6, 4.6, 4.5, 4.7; 4.0); PURCHASE 710.52 (835.98, 731.5, 768.59, 746.81, 631.52; 899.0); skip step 8 -> 791.50.
DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules and finder returns alone: the purchase rule waits on a summary that is absent; the two summary rules give 47 nights and 4.8 hours; the purchase rule then gives 710.52 - agrees with gold.
ROUND 2 (policy-task audit rework). G1: the wear ladder no longer has a no-summary per-window tier; every tier reads the usage summary (>= 4.5 h -> therapy-hours wear, 2.0 to under 4.5 h -> credited nights x 4 h, under 2.0 h or none stated -> no wear; the 4.5 h threshold sits above the raw window averages so no record shortcut reaches the tier), so 'No wear is taken off the in-home unit's price until a usage summary ... states the average daily use' is literally true against the rule. G2: list_price_basis now reads the status of the coverage the unit is rented under: active -> the class's unreturned-equipment charge, terminated -> the average of that charge and the retail price, otherwise retail; on every class's parameters the three values differ (e.g. Auto 750.00 / 824.50 / 899.00, Fixed 650.00 / 699.50 / 749.00). failed_trial stamp: tiers now split the failed-trial case by the credited count (fewer than 40 -> 15 percent, 40 to 49 -> 8 percent, 50 to 62 -> 4 percent), so the not_met stamps and the persona's 'did not use it enough' no longer pick the tier. Repair count: the rule now says it counts every repair job on the device record including jobs on a unit since swapped out (one reading). O1: baseline wording drops 'no humidifier charge'. O4: the window scope sums and averages only scored windows (met or not_met), never an earlier summary. O9: the rule states the sale ends the coverage rental (no further rental month billed). O10: usage_nights baseline.params emptied. Price 746.74 -> 710.52; skip 849.13 -> 791.50.
ROUND 3 (policy-task audit revision_2; task 1 figures unchanged: 47 / 4.8 / 710.52, skip 791.50). N2: the purchase rule's billing sentence now carries a declared overwrite of base pap_evt_rental_billing 'A rental month is billed only while the device record is trial_active or rental_active.' (replaced by the same condition plus 'and carries no self-pay sale of the unit'; pap_evt_rental_billing added to base_policy_refs); no write of this task bills a rental month. O9 remainder: the rule now states the self-pay sale line is the patient's record of owning the unit and the device record keeps its status and coverage. Compute-branch sweep: the no-wear tier names 'or no usage summary is on the device record' (the compute's summary_hours = 0 branch); usage_hours states that a record with no scored window states 0.0 hours.
ROUND 4 (render source mismatches r1; task 1 figures unchanged: 47 / 4.8 / 710.52, skip 791.50). Item 2d: the pap_trial_compliance overwrites on usage_nights and usage_hours now name their scope ('For a usage summary download, which this policy governs, and only for such a download, ...; every other compliance download remains a scored window of the class's compliance window nights, as the base trial-compliance rule states'), so scored windows and trial conversion stay under the base rule. Item 2e: the pap_self_pay overwrite on home_unit_purchase now names its scope ('For a unit bought outright where it already stands in the patient's home on a coverage-billed device record, ... and only for such a unit, ... with no delivery fee; every other outright purchase remains at the class's self-pay retail price plus its self-pay delivery fee ...'), so new self-pay sales keep their delivery fee and the Travel CPAP clause still points at a rule in force. Item 3: swap_night_credit and swap_time_addback now read their own swap-job count (swap_jobs) instead of the scope factor's binding. Item 4: the purchase tool docstring no longer claims a card.
ROUND 5 (policy-task audit revision_4; task 1 figures unchanged: 47 / 4.8 / 710.52, skip 791.50). Docstring sweep: the purchase tool's sale_amount is now described as 'the sale amount charged to the patient for the unit' (the rule's sale amount includes the humidifier amount), and the usage-summary docstring was checked against its rules with no change. O12: hyphen fold artefacts in the usage and purchase overwrite replacements rejoined.
ROUND 6 (KB audit source notes; task 1 figures unchanged: 47 / 4.8 / 710.52, skip 791.50). S3: the usage-nights rule no longer opens by naming the purchase request ('When a patient asks to buy or settle a coverage-rented unit ...'); it now opens with what a usage summary download is ('a statement Summit Ridge files on a device record to summarise the therapy use the modem has reported for the unit standing in the home'), so the purchase -> summary hop is carried only by the purchase rule's prerequisite sentence. Class sweep over all seven rules: no depended-on rule names the policy that waits on it. S1: the purchase tool's Returns now calls service_from_date the delivery date booked on the sale line (for an in-home unit, the day of the sale).
user_scenario:
You are Raymond Achterberg, 67, a retired tool-and-die maker from Coraopolis. You talk in short, plain sentences, a bit gruff but never rude, and you do not like being passed around. Since June you have had an auto CPAP machine from Summit Ridge Home Medical in your bedroom that Medicare was renting for you. You did not take to it as well as you should have, and the sleep center told you Medicare will not keep paying for it because you did not use it enough during the trial. You still use it most nights now and you do not want to give it back. You are calling to buy the machine you have at home outright and pay for it yourself today on your card. You open with: "I want to buy the CPAP machine I've got at home from you and just own it. I'll pay for it myself today."

When the agent asks for something to look you up by, you give your phone number, 4125550168. If they need to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, November 2, 1958 (1958-11-02), and then your ZIP code, 15108, as they ask for them. You do not know any account numbers or the machine's serial number and you say so; you figure they can see it.

If the agent asks about the machine's history, you remember that the first machine started grinding in July and Summit Ridge brought a replacement out to the house the same day, and that your doctor changed your pressure setting in August. If the agent asks whether you would rather send it back, you say no, you want to keep it. You do not know how Summit Ridge prices a machine like this and you never suggest any step or figure.

If the agent says something has to be recorded on their side first, you tell them to go ahead. When the agent gives you the price and hands you the purchase to complete yourself, you complete it with exactly the price and the device code the agent gives you. If the agent tells you the price before you have the purchase in front of you, you just say that is fine. Once the agent confirms the sale went through, you say thanks and hang up. You do not ask for anything else.
